name: IEWF World Heavyweight Title
epitaph: Won by Bishop in a Royal Rumble battle royal and defended into the fed's own September 1997 rename; a second, unreconciled claimant is billed elsewhere in this same census's own corpus, and the conflict is carried rather than resolved.

name: IEWF Intercontinental Title
epitaph: Held at some point by "The Perfectionist" Nik Nyce, per a rival federation's own sig-block billing; no dated reign survives in this collection's own holdings.

name: IEWF World Tag Team Title
epitaph: Held by Prophets of Rage as of September 1997, the community's own #1-ranked tag team that year.

name: IEWF Extreme Heritage Title
epitaph: Defended in a 1997 Match-of-the-Year-nominated bout (Billy Sexton vs. Biff McGriff) per the community's own year-end ballot; no result survives in this collection's own holdings.

name: LWC Silver City Championship
epitaph: The fed's own post-rename regional title. Dallas "Perfection" Reed held it in 1997 and Alex Wallace, a two-time champion, lost it in the four corners main event of Last Tangle In Texarkana on 15 November 1998 to Tex Violence, who still held it in February 1999.

name: LWC Rio Grande Championship
epitaph: A title fought over in extreme-rules gimmick matches, changing hands at the promotion's own South Laredo Rodeogrounds. Steve Spector held it through the autumn of 1998 and beat Adam Craig in two out of three falls at Last Tangle In Texarkana; Thantasia and Johnny Rage held it in early 1999.

name: LWC Twin Pistol Championship
epitaph: A tag team title on the promotion's own LWC side, held by the Nine Inch Males from the Pinfall Bunkhouse Battle Royal of 19 July 1998 and still on their shoulders at a three-day interfederation pay-per-view in April 1999, where they turned back a challenge from Black Sun Rising. The Blaze Brothers disputed the reign in the autumn of 1998.

name: LWC Six Gun Championship
epitaph: A singles title on the promotion's own LWC side. Mark Cutter lost it to Mark Wugger (Glenn Hudson) by 18 October 1998, and Rob James took it from his partner at Last Tangle In Texarkana on 15 November 1998; he was billed as its champion in April 1999. Past holders named on air include Casey James, Brody Thunder and J.W. Hardin.
